response.content:
## Defence and Drone Companies That Expanded to Sweden in 2026

Sweden's defence sector has seen significant expansion activity in 2026, driven by the country's NATO membership, rising military spending (projected at 2.8 % of GDP in 2026), and large-scale procurement programmes. Here are the key companies that expanded their presence or operations in Sweden during 2026:

### Major Defence Contractors

- **BAE Systems (UK)** — Invested over **$300 million** over five years at its **Hägglunds facility** in Örnsköldsvik, Sweden, to dramatically expand combat vehicle production capacity. Output at Hägglunds has surged 400 % since 2020 and headcount has more than tripled to 2,600. BAE Systems also expanded its **Bofors** artillery production in Karlskoga by 3–4×, and won a **$180 million** contract from Sweden's FMV for the **TRIDON Mk2** anti-aircraft gun system. It delivered the first **ARCHER** howitzers to Sweden under a broader $500 million contract.

- **Lockheed Martin (US)** — Secured a deal worth approximately **SEK 7 billion (~$650 million)** to supply Sweden with **HIMARS** rocket artillery systems, with deliveries starting in 2027. Lockheed Martin also signed a cooperation declaration with **Saab** to explore integration of Saab's Ground-Launched Small Diameter Bomb with HIMARS and joint munitions production for HIMARS and Patriot systems.

### Domestic Expansion (Drone & Counter-Drone)

- **Saab (Sweden)** — Won a **SEK 2.6 billion** (~$240 million) contract to develop and deliver a **counter-UAS (C-UAS) system** for the Swedish Armed Forces, with deliveries in 2027–2028. Saab is spending roughly **SEK 10 billion annually** on capacity expansion, scaling Giraffe 1X radar production beyond 300 units per year, and adding a new missile to the RBS 70 ground-based air defence system. Saab also partnered with **General Atomics (US)** on the **LoyalEye** unmanned airborne early warning system aboard the MQ-9B drone.

- **MilDef Group (Sweden)** — Europe's best-performing defence stock in 2026 (up over 80 %), focused on rugged computer systems and drone-related battlefield technology.

### Sweden's Broader Counter-Drone & Air Defence Investment

The Swedish government announced a total investment of **SEK 8.7 billion (~$916 million)** in air defence and anti-drone systems in 2026, with contracts going to Saab and BAE Systems among others. A separate **SEK 3.5 billion (~$367 million)** was earmarked specifically for counter-drone capabilities between 2026 and 2028. Sweden also established a new **defence industry cooperation office** and a **defence innovation unit** to attract further investment.

### Nordic & Allied Context

- Sweden and Ukraine signed a cooperation agreement to plan **joint defence production**, and Sweden joined a broader **Nordic common defence deal** initiative alongside Norway, Denmark, Finland, and Iceland (announced November 2026).
- **Draganfly (Canada/US)** expanded its footprint to meet Swedish defence customer demands, including search-and-rescue drone operations.

Sweden's rapid rearmament and NATO integration have made it one of Europe's most active defence-industry expansion destinations in 2026.

context.content: # BAE Systems awarded $180 million contract from Sweden for TRIDON Mk2. KARLSKOGA, Sweden, April 2, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BAE Systems has secured a contract worth $180 million from the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration (FMV) for the TRIDON Mk2 anti-aircraft system. BAE Systems has secured a contract worth $180 million from the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration for the TRIDON Mk2 anti-aircraft system. The TRIDON Mk2 is a truck-mounted 40 mm anti-aircraft gun system that addresses a gap in today's air defence. "The TRIDON Mk2 has been designed for today's warfare, and we will continue to deliver cutting-edge solutions to put our customers in the best position to meet future challenges.". In February, on behalf of Sweden and Denmark, the FMV procured TRIDON Mk2 systems to donate to Ukraine, as part of a package to bolster Ukraine's air defense capabilities. Able to combat multiple threats quickly, TRIDON Mk2 is a high-precision, cost-effective system that is easy to deploy and simple to maintain.

Finland already operates the Multiple Launch Rocket System, which shares munitions and components with HIMARS. That compatibility underpins the new Swedish-Finnish declaration, which extends beyond hardware to joint training, maintenance and production planning.

The agreement reflects a broader pattern of Nordic defence integration since Sweden and Finland joined NATO, as both governments align procurement choices to reinforce collective defence along Europe’s northern flank.

Sweden, like most European countries, is ​racing to bolster its defences following Russia's invasion of Ukraine with military spending projected to hit 2.8% of GDP in 2026, rising to 3.5% in 2030. Defence Minister Pal Jonson said the ‌added capability would ⁠help broaden Sweden's air defences, which are at present chiefly focused on protecting military units. Jonson added that the systems had been tested on the battlefield in Ukraine and had proved very effective against drones like the Shahed model used by ‌Russia and Iran. Saab said in a ​separate statement that their part of ​the package amounted to ​2.6 billion crowns and was for its anti-drone ‌platform designed to detect and ​neutralise low-flying small- ​to medium-sized drones.

"I think the 2014 annexation of Crimea was when we saw something starting to happen," he told ‌Reuters at the Hagglunds test track in ⁠Ornskoldsvik, adding that it all took off just before Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine. Sweden's arms exports have more than tripled to 28 billion crowns ($3.02 billion) in 2025, from 8 billion in 2015. The defence industry employs around 30,000 people in Sweden, most of them at Saab, maker ​of ​the Gripen fighter jet and the A-26 submarine. Output has surged 400% since 2020 and headcount has more than tripled to 2,600 from 800, making Hagglunds by far the biggest employer in the town of just 56,000.
